p25.paper_title: Conflict as an Inverse of Attention in Sequence Relationship

claims.source_quote: we show that attention, by virtue of its composition, works best only when it is given that there is a match somewhere between two sequences. It does not very well adapt to cases when there is no similarity between two sequences or if the relationship is contrastive.
claims.true_claim: Attention works best when there is a match between two sequences and struggles when the relationship between sequences is contrastive or non-similar.
claims.perturbed_claim: Attention works best when there is no match between two sequences and struggles when the relationship between sequences is highly similar.

claims.source_quote: a standard dot-product based attention with softmax won't be able to produce weights which is below 0.33 (=1/3) for all the words in the second sequence with respect to the word "height" in the first sequence.
claims.true_claim: When a query word has no matching word in a three-word target sequence, dot-product attention with softmax cannot assign weights below 0.33 to all target words simultaneously.
claims.perturbed_claim: When a query word has no matching word in a three-word target sequence, dot-product attention with softmax cannot assign weights below 0.25 to all target words simultaneously.

claims.source_quote: Our approach consists of using element wise difference between two vectors followed by a linear transformation to produce a scalar weight.
claims.true_claim: The conflict model computes dissimilarity between word pairs using element-wise difference between vectors followed by a linear transformation to produce a scalar weight.
claims.perturbed_claim: The conflict model computes dissimilarity between word pairs using element-wise multiplication between vectors followed by a linear transformation to produce a scalar weight.

claims.source_quote: We particularly focused on the examples which were incorrectly marked in attention model but correctly in attention-conflict model. claims.true_claim: Among examples that the attention-only model got wrong but the attention-conflict model got right, 70% were cases where the attention-only model falsely labeled a non-duplicate pair as duplicate.
claims.perturbed_claim: Among examples that the attention-only model got wrong but the attention-conflict model got right, 70% were cases where the attention-only model falsely labeled a duplicate pair as non-duplicate.
